title: The Dead Sea: Lowest Place on Land
summary: Why the Dead Sea is the lowest place on land, why its water is so salty that people float, why almost nothing lives in it, and why it is shrinking.
poll: People should work hard to save the Dead Sea from shrinking.

versions.title: The Dead Sea
versions.text:
Most land is high up. But one spot is very low. It is the Dead Sea. It is the lowest place on land.

The Dead Sea is not a real sea. It is a big lake. It is not far from Saudi Arabia. The land there is hot and dry.

The lake is full of salt. It has lots more salt than the sea. You can see white salt on the shore. It looks like ice!

The salt does a fun thing. It helps you float! You do not sink. You can lie back and read a book on top of the lake.

Why is it called dead? No fish can live in it. No plants grow in it. It is too salty. Just tiny germs live there.

A river runs into the lake. But no river runs out. The hot sun dries up the water. The salt stays in the lake.

Now the lake is shrinking. People use the river for farms. They use it at home, too. So less water gets in. Each year, the lake gets a bit smaller.

versions.title: The Dead Sea: Lowest Place on Land
versions.text:
Most land on Earth is higher than the ocean. But the shore of the Dead Sea is more than 430 meters below sea level. That makes it the lowest place on land in the world.

The Dead Sea is not really a sea. It is a large salt lake that lies in a deep valley in the Middle East, northwest of Saudi Arabia. The weather there is hot and dry, and it rarely rains.

The water is about ten times saltier than the ocean. White salt crystals cover the rocks along the shore. All this salt makes the water very dense, or heavy for its size. Because of this, people float easily on the surface. Visitors often lie back and read a newspaper while floating!

No fish or plants can live in such salty water. Only microbes, tiny living things that are too small to see, survive there. This is how the lake got its name.

How did the lake become so salty? The Jordan River carries water and minerals into the lake, but no river flows out. In the hot sun, the water evaporates into the air. The salt and minerals stay behind, so the water becomes saltier over time.

Today, the Dead Sea is shrinking. People take water from the Jordan River for farms and cities, so less water reaches the lake. Companies also dry out lake water to collect minerals. The water level drops more than one meter every year. As the water moves back, deep holes called sinkholes open up in the ground near the shore.

versions.title: The Dead Sea: Lowest Place on Land
versions.text:
Most land on Earth is higher than the ocean, but the shore of the Dead Sea lies more than 430 meters below sea level, which makes it the lowest elevation on land anywhere in the world.

Despite its name, the Dead Sea is not actually a sea. It is an enormous salt lake located in a deep valley in the Middle East, northwest of Saudi Arabia, where the climate is extremely hot and dry and rainfall is unusual.

The lake has a salt concentration of about 34 percent, approximately ten times higher than that of the ocean, and white salt crystals decorate the rocks along the shore. This extraordinary amount of dissolved salt makes the water exceptionally dense, so the human body is buoyant enough to float effortlessly on the surface. Visitors frequently relax on their backs while reading a newspaper!

No fish or plants can survive in such salty water. Only microbes, microscopic organisms such as certain bacteria, are able to live there, which explains how the lake received its name.

Although nothing lives in its water, the lake is valuable to people in other ways. Tourists from many countries visit its shores, and some cover their skin with the dark mud found there, which is rich in minerals and is used in skin-care products. Factories also take magnesium and bromine from the water.

The lake became so salty because the Jordan River carries water and dissolved minerals into it, but no river flows out. Under the intense sun, the water evaporates into the atmosphere, while the salt and minerals remain behind, and over thousands of years the concentration gradually increased.

Today, however, the Dead Sea is shrinking rapidly. Communities divert water from the Jordan River for agriculture and expanding cities, so less water reaches the lake. Industrial companies also evaporate lake water in enormous ponds for the extraction of valuable minerals, such as potash for fertilizer. Consequently, the water level drops more than one meter every year. As the shoreline retreats, thousands of dangerous sinkholes have opened in the ground nearby, damaging roads and buildings.
